blocks.title: Class NP
blocks.text: Class NP (Non-deterministic Polynomial time) is the set of problems for which a proposed solution can be checked quickly by a computer, although finding a solution may be difficult and time-consuming.

Example: Sudoku. A 9 x 9 grid is filled so that every row, column and 3 x 3 subgrid contains the digits 1 to 9 exactly once. Checking a completed grid is easy: look at each row, column and subgrid for repeats. Solving a puzzle from scratch can need a lot of trial and error or an advanced algorithm, and there is no simple fast method that always works.
